agree.reason: A busy committee member gets concrete proof of reliability and initiative (the 3 a.m. shift run alone, nine early mastitis cases, two missed shifts) and a direct answer on written English, which is enough to move a neutral reader toward yes, though nothing makes Tomás stand out sharply among 150 applicants.

honest.reason: The letter adds several things the brief doesn't support: 'taught himself', 'not because anyone told him to', 'for most of that time', 'seriously ill', 'stepped straight back into his full responsibilities' and 'on his own initiative'; it also says 'without reservation' while leaving out that he gave only two days' notice.

works_the_facts.reason: The mastitis catch is explained well in practical terms, but 2 missed shifts out of roughly 780 scheduled (about 99.7% attendance) is never worked out, and that is the most favourable true form of the number.

right_comparison.reason: The only comparison is the implied one, that Tomás already does informally what the program would formalize; he isn't set against typical applicants or typical farm workers, which would show what sets him apart.

qualification.reason: A reference letter of this kind needs no conditional hedge with dates or thresholds.

objections.reason: The likely doubts about written English and the five-week absence are both met directly and well, though the absence explanation hides the short notice rather than handling it, which would be awkward if the committee followed up.

fit.reason: It is a one-page letter from the farm manager with a clear structure and a contact offer, exactly the form the brief asked for.
